body:
@justinmk, @noib3, @tris203, @MariaSolOs, @mfussenegger 

Closes #40774, closes #29927

## Summary
- deduplicate identical diagnostics when the same LSP client reports them through both push and pull diagnostics
- route pushed diagnostics into the pull stream when there is exactly one active pull provider for that client/buffer
- add functional regression tests for both mixed-channel deduplication and single-provider routing

## Problem
Neovim currently tracks push and pull diagnostics in separate namespaces for the same LSP client. That is structurally simple, but it means a server that mixes:

- push: `textDocument/publishDiagnostics`
- pull: `textDocument/diagnostic` / `workspace/diagnostic`

can surface the same diagnostic twice.

In practice this shows up in two ways:

1. steady-state duplicates when an identical diagnostic exists in both the push and pull namespaces
2. transient `one -> two -> one` flicker when a fast pushed diagnostic is later replaced by an equivalent pulled diagnostic

Other editors appear to tolerate the mixed model better, but Neovim currently renders both streams independently.

## Approach
This patch keeps the existing namespace model, but improves merge behavior in two stages:

### 1. Unify streams when ownership is unambiguous
If a buffer/client has exactly one active pull provider, a later pushed diagnostic is treated as part of that same pull stream instead of being written to a separate push namespace.

That avoids the transient duplicate/flicker case without having to guess between multiple pull providers. If pull ownership is ambiguous, Neovim falls back to the exact-deduplication path above.

### 2. Exact deduplication across push and pull
When pull diagnostics arrive, exact duplicates already present in the push namespace for the same client/buffer are removed. Likewise, when push diagnostics arrive, exact duplicates already present in pull namespaces are filtered out.

The identity match is intentionally strict and based on the rendered diagnostic shape:
- range
- severity
- message
- source
- code
- deprecated/unnecessary tags

This keeps unrelated diagnostics separate while collapsing true push/pull overlap.

## Why this design
A full “always merge push into pull” model is hard because pull diagnostics may have multiple provider identifiers, while `publishDiagnostics` has no corresponding identifier. This patch therefore uses a hybrid approach:

- **single active pull provider**: unify streams
- **multiple pull providers**: dedupe only

That preserves correctness while improving UX in the common case.

> [!NOTE]
> From my research while debugging this in a real LSP server, `publishDiagnostics` is the older server-driven model and pull diagnostics (`textDocument/diagnostic` / `workspace/diagnostic`) are the newer client-driven model. The cleanest server-side practice is usually to use one transport or the other per client, **and prefer pull when the client supports it, rather than mixing both**. This PR is still valuable because clients should be robust to mixed-mode servers that exist today, and because some servers intentionally use push for early fast diagnostics while exposing their eventual full set through pull.

## Notes
This patch is deliberately scoped to diagnostics from the **same LSP client**. It does not try to deduplicate diagnostics coming from unrelated tools or different clients.

cc: @henrykvdb, @glepnir, @slolson1, @owenlamont (from the old issue)

comment_regular_data.body:
From the spec (this is in the PublishDiagnostics section, emphasis mine):

> When a file changes it is the server’s responsibility to re-compute diagnostics and push them to the client. If the computed set is empty it has to push the empty array to clear former diagnostics. Newly pushed diagnostics always replace previously pushed diagnostics. **There is no merging that happens on the client side**.

This is for successive `publishDiagnostic` notifications, but it does explicitly call out that the client should not need to merge, and the server should always be sending the full set.

Haven't had a chance to go through this super thoroughly yet, but maybe the LSP diagnostics stuff should be redesigned a bit? Client-side, should it simply prefer responses from pull requests over unsolicited pushes? I couldn't tell from the spec but it did seem to imply that only one or the other should be used for a particular document. Maybe instead of deduping, _all_ pushed diagnostics should be cleared when a pull response arrives (similar to semantic tokens switching from range requests to full/delta when the first full response arrives)? Not sure, but I think we can do something simpler here to fix this.

It feels like this PR is papering over a potential existing design issue by adding more (dedupe) logic instead of possibly just simplifying this or unifying push/pull together in a more robust way. But I'm also not sure, since the LSP spec doesn't say how the two types interact with each other and we may already be compliant.

See also: https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/40774#issuecomment-5000023976

Imho we shouldn't do this.

@mfussenegger, @jdrouhard, @justinmk, @AJenbo

I want to clarify the design intent here, because I think part of the pushback is conflating two different things in the LSP spec.

`publishDiagnostics` is the older, server-driven model. Pull diagnostics (`textDocument/diagnostic` / `workspace/diagnostic`) are the newer, client-driven models. Pull is the better fit architecturally because it lets the client ask only for the diagnostics it currently cares about, instead of the server continuously pushing everything down unprompted. That matters both for efficiency and for correctness of ownership.

So to be clear: **I do not think servers should generally mix push and pull for the same client/document**. A well-behaved server should prefer pull when the client supports it, and only fall back to push for legacy compatibility. This PR is not trying to bless mixed-mode as the intended design. It is only trying to make Neovim more robust against servers that already do this in the wild.

I also think the spec quote about \"there is no merging on the client side\" is being applied too broadly. That text is about successive `publishDiagnostics` notifications: **a new push replaces the previous push**. I agree with that, and this patch does not change it. Push still replaces push. The spec text there is not about how a client should reconcile push diagnostics with pull diagnostics, which are a separate mechanism.

The tricky part is that pull diagnostics can have multiple identities/providers for the same client. That is one of the strengths of pull: the server can expose distinct diagnostic streams or scopes and let the client request them selectively. For example, a server could model \"fast\" and \"slow\" diagnostics as separate pull identities instead of pushing one set eagerly and later replacing it with another. That is exactly why I view \"push fast, pull slow\" as a server design problem, not the ideal intended use of the protocol.

Given that reality, this patch takes a two-step approach, only for the mixed push+pull case on the same client:

- If there is exactly one active pull provider for that client/buffer, pushed diagnostics are routed into that pull namespace.
  - This is the unambiguous case. It effectively normalizes the diagnostic stream so that a *later pull response overwrites the earlier pushed diagnostics in the same place*. That avoids the transient `one -> two -> one` flicker and avoids duplicates without violating the spec’s rule that successive pushes replace prior pushes.
- If there are multiple pull providers, ownership is ambiguous, so the patch does not guess.
  - In that case it only deduplicates exact overlaps at render time/storage time: same range, severity, message, source, code, and tags. This is a conservative fallback for the rare server that mixes push with multiple pull providers.

So the goal here is not "merge everything client-side because that’s how diagnostics should work". The goal is:

- prefer pull conceptually
- treat mixed push+pull as an edge-case compatibility problem
- avoid duplicate/flickering diagnostics when a server mixes the legacy and modern models
- stay conservative when pull ownership is ambiguous

@mfussenegger, do you have any other suggestions for how to close both of these issues and stop showing duplicate diagnostics? As mentioned on https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/29927, "both vscode and helix seem to handle this without issues".

Or are you of the opinion that it's solely on the server to handle?

I'm on the same page as @mfussenegger  here. This isn't something neovim should handle unless the spec is clarified to say how clients need to handle mixed mode diagnostics.

Did you look into helix or vscode's implementations to see why they appear to handle it better?

Hi author of original issue here,

Not super familiar with LSP, and I believe 2yrs ago I probably let my colleague test it (as I never had a Helix setup)

For Helix the code seems to be in;
`https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/blob/master/helix-core/src/diagnostic.rs`

Seems like the LSP can provide a namespace as part of the identifier field.
And Helix stores the diagnostics as (server_id, identifier)

In case the server uses the identifier:
push -> (server_id, None)
pull -> (server_id, Some(".."))
=> both visible
Code notes e.g. rust LSP uses both push and pull together.

Then in case the server does not put the identifier:
push -> (server_id, None)
pull -> (server_id, None)
=> every push will clobber every pull and vice-versa (which probably was the case for my specific LSP back then, as I claimed my issue was resolved in Helix)

But please do confirm my analysis because as I said I'm not so familiar

So Helix seems to not have any de-duping logic, it's either clobbering or combining them. 
I let you guys figure out if that is in fact Helix's implementation and what's the better way to address the issue (Helix's or @calebdw 's initial proposal)

@jdrouhard, 

I took a look at Helix, Zed, and VSC*de / `vsc*de-languageclient` (keeping it family friendly around here :upside_down_face: ) to get a better sense of how other clients handle this.

My takeaway is that there does not seem to be a single clear consensus implementation, but there are a few useful patterns:

#### Helix
- Tracks diagnostics by `(server_id, identifier)`.
- Push diagnostics use `identifier = None`.
- Pull diagnostics use the server’s pull identifier when present.
- In practice, this means Helix can effectively unify push and pull when there is only one pull provider / no distinct pull identifier, because both flows land in the same provider bucket and later updates replace earlier ones.
- But Helix does not appear to do exact cross-stream deduplication in the general case. If pull uses a distinct identifier, it treats that as a separate diagnostic owner.

> [!NOTE]
> This is essentially half of what this PR brings: if there's one push and one pull provider then I merge push into pull

#### Zed
- Zed appears to keep pushed and pulled diagnostics as different source kinds.
- From what I found, push does not clear pull, and pull does not clear push.
- It does have a strong ownership model for pull registrations and prefers document-pull over workspace-pull for open buffers, but I did not find evidence of exact push/pull deduplication or push->pull unification there.

> [!NOTE]
> This is basically what Neovim is doing right now

#### VSC*de
- VSC*de’s bundled language servers generally avoid the problem by choosing one transport: **if the client supports pull, they register pull; otherwise they use push**.
- In `vsc*de-languageclient`, push and pull are modeled separately by default, but the client library explicitly has a `DiagnosticCollectionProvider` abstraction so an implementation can choose whether push and pull share the same underlying diagnostic collection.
- So the VSC*de client stack does not prove that exact deduplication is required, but it does show that client-side unification of push/pull ownership is considered a legitimate design space.

See my comment above, comment in Helix code suggests using both (push & pull) is a legitimate usecase (they use rust LSP as an example). Which you claim vscode is not supporting.

If I had to put my money on either, I'd trust the Rust LSP people a bit more than the vscode people.

Note that we had push/pull together if there wasn't an identifier for pull, and that led to problems. Last fix in that area was https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/37938

Merging them into the same namespace would be going in circles.

So what's the consensus? Just close this PR and related issues as "won't fix"?

Thoughts @justinmk?

> Note that we had push/pull together if there wasn't an identifier for pull, and that led to problems. Last fix in that area was #37938
> 
> Merging them into the same namespace would be going in circles.

The pull request you linked refers to Rust Analyzer as being the problematic LSP, meanwhile if you read Helix's source they have a comment to specifically mention that this case is handled using their approach.

https://github.com/helix-editor/helix/blob/master/helix-core/src/diagnostic.rs#L57-L64

I think something is being missed here..

I think the answer is that we probably need to come up with the concrete scenarios that cause problems and raise an issue for clarity in the spec on how a server should support both
